subject: digger wasp
title: A Scientist Fooled This Wasp 40 Times in a Row With the Same Trick

scenes.text: A scientist fooled this wasp forty times in a row, with the same trick.
The Sphex wasp stings a cricket so it's paralysed but still alive, then drags it home.
At the burrow, it drops the cricket at the door and goes inside to check.
Jean-Henri Fabre slid the cricket a few inches away while the wasp was inside.
The wasp came out, dragged it back to the door, and went in to check all over again.
Forty times, the same wasp, the same check. It never just pulled the cricket in.

description:
The French naturalist Jean-Henri Fabre moved a Sphex wasp's paralysed cricket a few inches every time the wasp went into its burrow to inspect it.
One wasp repeated the whole routine forty times. Its larva later feeds on the living, paralysed cricket.
Would you call that instinct or stubbornness?
first_comment: Later experiments found some wasps give up and drag the cricket straight in after a few tries. How many times would you check?
